Fact.Name: Look-back interest for this year, with section-specific accrual and rate rules: cumulative daily compound factor numerator
Fact.Description: Interest-only factor, excluding principal, from a retained daily-compounding computation for the stated accrual interval. Enter numerator and denominator explicitly; annual simple interest rates are not a substitute. The rate is the adjusted overpayment rate (section 167(g)(2)(C), which takes its definition from section 460(b)(7)) for BOTH directions: a hypothetical underpayment (tax increase on line 6) and a hypothetical overpayment (tax decrease) accrue at the same overpayment rate, never the underpayment rate. For each interest accrual period, which runs from the day after the prior year's return due date (not including extensions) to the next year's return due date, the rate is the section 6621(a)(1) overpayment rate in effect on the first day of that period and stays fixed for the whole period even though the published rates change quarterly; interest is compounded daily.

Fact.Name: Form 8866 lines 9b to 9d: direct deposit account for the separate refund
Fact.Description: Form 8866 lines 9b (routing number), 9c (Checking or Savings) and 9d (account number): the account for a direct deposit of the net look-back interest refund claimed on the separately filed form (/form8866SeparateRefundClaim). The same validated BankAccount type paymentMethod:/bankAccount and form8697:/form8697RefundBankAccount use, so the instructions' rules ride on the type: the routing number is nine digits whose first two are 01 through 12 or 21 through 32, the account number is up to 17 characters, and exactly one account type is chosen. Leave it unanswered for a refund by check.
